While doing newidle load balancing
column2: it is possible for new tasks to

column1: arrive
column2: such as with pending wakeups. newidle_balance() already accounts

column1: for this by exiting the sched_domain load_balance() iteration if it
detects these cases. This is very important for minimizing wakeup
latency.
However
column2: if we are already in load_balance()
column3: we may stay there for a

column1: while before returning back to newidle_balance(). This is most
exacerbated if we enter a 'goto redo' loop in the LBF_ALL_PINNED case. A
very straightforward workaround to this is to adjust should_we_balance()
to bail out if we're doing a CPU_NEWLY_IDLE balance and new tasks are
detected.
This was tested with the following reproduction:
- two threads that take turns sleeping and waking each other up are
affined to two cores
- a large number of threads with 100% utilization are pinned to all
other cores
Without this patch
column2: wakeup latency was ~120us for the pair of threads

column1: almost entirely spent in load_balance(). With this patch
is ~6us.
